DeployBot: [PROD] Rollout initiated by @release_mgr — tag v3.2.1, commit `abc1234`, canary=10% :rocket:
release_mgr: kicking off canary, migration flag is OFF. rolling out traffic to canary pool now.
Emma L: quick q — are we pinning the inference model for this release or using latest autosync?
Sanjeev K: pinned in overlay to `open-llama-13b-quant` for this tag. config diff pushed to release branch.
Carla Ops: change window confirmed until 22:00 UTC. monitoring and alerts prewarmed.
DeployBot: Canary health check: 10/10 sample responses OK, latency p95=120ms, error rate=0.2%. No deployment-blocking alerts.
Emma L: glanced at samples, outputs look correct. :thumbsup:
release_mgr: okay to proceed to ramp to 50% unless anyone objects.
Sanjeev K: no objections from infra side — autoscaler behaving as expected.
DeployBot: Scaling to 50% (ramp step) — new pods coming up, image tag v3.2.1.
Carla Ops: watch on DB connections during ramp, we're at 85% of pooled DB connections. throttling configured.
DeployBot: Halfway health snapshot — p95=130ms, errors=0.18%, KV cache hit rate 74%.
Emma L: running one more smoke test against a pinned prompt set — started.
Emma L: smoke pass ✅ no semantic regressions in the sampled prompts.
DeployBot: Rolling out remaining 50% — entering final phase.
Sanjeev K: noted: rollout includes a small config tweak to batching window. slowed token batching by 10ms to reduce lat tail.
DeployBot: Rollout complete — 100% of production serving tag v3.2.1 (commit `abc1234`). Duration: 16m16s. Job: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/12345 :white_check_mark:
release_mgr: nice work. I'll update the release notes and ping engineering channels.
Carla Ops: monitoring slate for 30m post-deploy. Will escalate if any SLO alerts trip.
DeployBot: Post-rollout metrics snapshot: p95=125ms, errors=0.25%, no regressions flagged by automated evals.
Emma L: adding a follow-up ticket to verify long-tail prompts in nightly run.
Sanjeev K: will cherry-pick the batching tweak into next canary branch.
release_mgr: thanks everyone — closing thread.
